content.text:
The drawing shows a 3,4-dihydronaphthalen-1(2H)-one (tetralone) core. The aromatic ring is fused to a saturated six-membered ring that carries the ketone. A phenyl group (Ph) sits on the aromatic carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon that bears the C=O carbon, which makes it position 8.

Atom by atom:
- The carbonyl carbon C1 has a C=O and is bonded to the aromatic ring-fusion carbon C8a.
- C8a is bonded to C8, which carries the phenyl group.
- The ring continues C8, C7, C6, C5, then C4a, the other fusion carbon.
- C4a connects to CH2 (C4), then CH2 (C3), then CH2 (C2), and back to C1.

SMILES: O=C1CCCc2cccc(-c3ccccc3)c12

Check: C1(=O) is followed by CCC for C2, C3 and C4. Then c2 is C4a, and ccc are C5, C6 and C7. Next, c(-Ph) is C8, and c12 is C8a, which closes the aromatic ring (label 2) and the ketone ring (label 1). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1CCCc2cccc(-c3ccccc3)c12
